study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Rehák Bučková et al., eLife Reviewed Preprint, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative models pre-trained on cross-sectional data to evaluate intra-individual longitudinal changes in neuroimaging data

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Extend cross-sectional normative modelling to longitudinal designs by introducing a z-diff score that quantifies whether an individual’s change between two visits exceeds expected healthy change using pre-trained normative models, and demonstrate the method in early-stage schizophrenia.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group-level Wilcoxon tests on z-diff with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control; ANCOVA for thickness (visit 2 as DV) with group (patients vs controls) adjusting for age, sex, and baseline thickness; PCA of z-diff across IDPs (10 components) followed by Spearman correlations with changes in PANSS and GAF.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Compared to cross-sectional analyses, z-diff revealed significant longitudinal normalisation of frontal cortical thickness in early-stage schizophrenia; PCA-derived z-diff components correlated with functional (GAF) and symptom (PANSS) changes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using z-diff scores, the study identified significant normalisation in frontal cortex regions between visits, including bilateral superior frontal sulcus, bilateral middle frontal sulcus, bilateral middle frontal gyrus, and right superior frontal gyrus (FDR-corrected). Cross-sectional analyses showed lower cortical thickness in patients at the first visit relative to healthy populations. PCA of z-diff (10 components) showed the first component (reflecting global thickness change) correlated with GAF change, and the second component correlated with PANSS change (see Fig. 7).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Site-specific adaptation can be omitted if longitudinal controls are scarce since offsets cancel when taking differences, but healthy longitudinal change variance still needs estimation; implementation provided via PCNtoolkit tutorial; results caution against naïve subtraction of two z-scores for longitudinal inference.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional normative models do not encode individual longitudinal dynamics, so z-diff relies on estimating healthy-change variance and may be conservative when autocorrelation is low or measurement noise is high; external-domain validation was not performed; parcellation-level details are not exhaustively specified.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Scanner: Siemens MAGNETOM Prisma 3T; T1 MPRAGE with 0.7 mm slices (TR=2400 ms; TE=2.34 ms; TI=1000 ms; flip=8°; 320×320). Median Rho across IDPs ~0.30 (visit 1) and 0.26 (visit 2).
